<div class="sphinxpress-doc">
<section id="why-pyjev">
<h1>Why pyjev?</h1>
<p>The official <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">typesafe-sdk</span></code> is the right tool for making TypeSafe System One
requests. <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">pyjev</span></code> is useful when a judgment should become a reusable part of an
application rather than remain an inline request.</p>
<blockquote>
<div><p><strong>The SDK executes System One requests. pyjev turns recurring Jev judgments
into inspectable, reusable decision contracts and application workflows.</strong></p>
</div></blockquote>
<p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">pyjev</span></code> is a decision-engineering layer over the official Python SDK. It keeps the
SDK as the transport and model boundary, while adding source-controlled decision
contracts, offline inspection and fingerprints, reusable policy gates, semantic
recipes, batch/output tooling, and a consistent contract across Python, shell,
CI, and agent workflows.</p>
<section id="the-sdk-is-the-execution-layer">
<h2>The SDK is the execution layer</h2>
<p>TypeSafe and Jev provide the model semantics and API. <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">typesafe-sdk</span></code> provides the
Python request and response models, synchronous and asynchronous clients,
transport, retries, authentication, assets, and API errors. Those are SDK
responsibilities, not pyjev’s differentiators.</p>
<div class="highlight-text notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span>TypeSafe / Jev
  model semantics and API

  typesafe-sdk
    request/response models, clients, transport, retries, assets,
    authentication, and API errors

    pyjev
      declaration -&gt; validation -&gt; inspection -&gt; execution
                   -&gt; interpretation -&gt; caller policy

  application
    effects and business decisions
</pre></div>
</div>
<p>A raw SDK call is often the simplest answer to “make this System One request.”
The SDK remains the baseline and the low-level escape hatch. pyjev delegates
execution to it rather than creating a second transport stack.</p>
</section>
<section id="pyjev-is-the-decision-contract-layer">
<h2>pyjev is the decision-contract layer</h2>
<p>A recurring judgment can have a stable identity in <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">.pyjev.toml</span></code>. The contract
can then be validated, compiled, reviewed, executed, and interpreted consistently
by different parts of an application and its automation.</p>
<div class="highlight-text notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span>declare       .pyjev.toml
validate      pyjev decision validate
inspect       pyjev decision compile &lt;name&gt; --state ...
review        source control + deterministic specification fingerprint
execute       Jev.decide(...) | AsyncJev.decide(...) | pyjev decide ...
interpret     typed result | local pipeline | CLI output/gate
</pre></div>
</div>
<p>For example, a <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">ticket-route</span></code> decision can be used from application code and
shell/CI without duplicating its Choice criteria:</p>
<div class="highlight-toml notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="k">[decision.ticket-route]</span>
<span class="n">type</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&quot;choice&quot;</span>
<span class="n">question</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&quot;Which team should handle this support request?&quot;</span>

<span class="k">[decision.ticket-route.options]</span>
<span class="n">billing</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&quot;Billing or refunds&quot;</span>
<span class="n">engineering</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&quot;Technical problem or product bug&quot;</span>
<span class="n">sales</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&quot;Purchasing or procurement&quot;</span>
</pre></div>
</div>
<div class="highlight-python notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="kn">from</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nn">pyjev</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kn">import</span> <span class="n">Jev</span>

<span class="k">with</span> <span class="n">Jev</span><span class="p">()</span> <span class="k">as</span> <span class="n">jev</span><span class="p">:</span>
    <span class="n">result</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">jev</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">decide</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s2">&quot;ticket-route&quot;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">state</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="n">ticket</span><span class="p">)</span>
</pre></div>
</div>
<div class="highlight-bash notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="nb">printf</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s1">&#39;%s&#39;</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&quot;</span><span class="nv">$ticket</span><span class="s2">&quot;</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">|</span><span class="w"> </span>pyjev<span class="w"> </span>decide<span class="w"> </span>ticket-route<span class="w"> </span>--json
</pre></div>
</div>
<p>The value is not shorter syntax for an SDK request. The judgment now has a
version-controlled project identity that can be inspected and reused.</p>
</section>
<section id="what-changes-when-a-judgment-becomes-application-infrastructure">
<h2>What changes when a judgment becomes application infrastructure</h2>
<section id="give-it-a-stable-identity">
<h3>Give it a stable identity</h3>
<p>Named Noul, Choice, Score, and bundle decisions live in <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">.pyjev.toml</span></code>. A stable
name makes the declaration reusable and reviewable instead of repeating its
criteria in each call site.</p>
</section>
<section id="inspect-it-without-credentials">
<h3>Inspect it without credentials</h3>
<p><code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">pyjev</span> <span class="pre">decision</span> <span class="pre">validate</span></code> and <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">compile_decision()</span></code> validate declarations and
produce a normalized request preview without constructing a client, reading
credentials, or contacting the API. The compiled representation includes a
stable fingerprint for the validated decision specification. It can support
review, snapshots, distinguishing specification changes from runtime state, and
machine-readable code-review or deployment checks. It is not tamper-proofing or a
persisted audit log.</p>
</section>
<section id="reuse-it-across-python-and-automation">
<h3>Reuse it across Python and automation</h3>
<p>A named contract can be run through <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">Jev</span></code> or <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">AsyncJev</span></code>, or invoked from the CLI
in shell and CI. That gives the application one declaration and consistent
pyjev-level result and gate conventions across runtime surfaces.</p>
</section>
<section id="preserve-uncertainty">
<h3>Preserve uncertainty</h3>
<p>pyjev result wrappers retain applicable values, confidence or probability
distributions, usage, model, raw response data, and request ID. They provide a
stable pyjev-facing result contract across decisions, recipes, pipelines, CLI
serialization, and batch tooling. The underlying SDK remains responsible for its
own typed request and response models. Confidence and probabilities are signals,
not guarantees of correctness.</p>
</section>
<section id="separate-judgment-from-policy">
<h3>Separate judgment from policy</h3>
<p>Python pipelines apply thresholds to an already returned result. CLI confidence
gates provide an automation contract: a valid low-confidence Choice or Score can
exit with code <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">3</span></code> without emitting an actionable <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">--value</span></code>. Thresholds and
follow-up actions belong to the caller. A rejected policy gate is not an API
failure, and the pipeline does not execute side effects.</p>
</section>
<section id="package-common-semantic-workflows">
<h3>Package common semantic workflows</h3>
<p>Recipes package deterministic planning, Jev execution through the caller’s
client, and deterministic interpretation. For example, <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">extract</span></code> finds literal
candidates in Python, asks Jev to select only among those candidates or <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">none</span></code>,
then preserves evidence for deterministic normalization and caller-owned review
policy. <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">find</span></code> separates candidate ranking from applicability. <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">verify</span></code>
distinguishes support, contradiction, and no evidence. <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">route</span></code> returns a typed
proposal and never invokes handlers.</p>
<p>The <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">build</span> <span class="pre">-&gt;</span> <span class="pre">execute</span> <span class="pre">-&gt;</span> <span class="pre">interpret</span></code> split makes request shape, call count, policy
inputs, and result interpretation easier to inspect and test separately from the
network call. See <a class="reference internal" href="../recipes/"><span class="std std-doc">Semantic recipes</span></a>.</p>
</section>
</section>
<section id="a-side-by-side-example">
<h2>A side-by-side example</h2>
<p>A direct SDK call is appropriate when the route is simply implementation code:</p>
<div class="highlight-python notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="kn">from</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nn">typesafe_sdk</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kn">import</span> <span class="n">Choice</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">TypeSafeClient</span>

<span class="k">with</span> <span class="n">TypeSafeClient</span><span class="p">()</span> <span class="k">as</span> <span class="n">client</span><span class="p">:</span>
    <span class="n">response</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">client</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">system_one</span><span class="p">(</span>
        <span class="n">state</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="n">ticket</span><span class="p">,</span>
        <span class="n">questions</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="p">{</span>
            <span class="s2">&quot;route&quot;</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="n">Choice</span><span class="p">(</span>
                <span class="n">instructions</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s2">&quot;Which team should handle this support request?&quot;</span><span class="p">,</span>
                <span class="n">criteria</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="p">{</span>
                    <span class="s2">&quot;billing&quot;</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="s2">&quot;Billing or refunds&quot;</span><span class="p">,</span>
                    <span class="s2">&quot;engineering&quot;</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="s2">&quot;Technical problem or product bug&quot;</span><span class="p">,</span>
                    <span class="s2">&quot;sales&quot;</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="s2">&quot;Purchasing or procurement&quot;</span><span class="p">,</span>
                <span class="p">},</span>
            <span class="p">)</span>
        <span class="p">},</span>
    <span class="p">)</span>

<span class="n">route</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">response</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">choices</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="s2">&quot;route&quot;</span><span class="p">]</span>
</pre></div>
</div>
<p>With pyjev, the recurring judgment can instead be declared once, inspected
without credentials, fingerprinted, and shared with CLI automation:</p>
<div class="highlight-toml notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="k">[decision.ticket-route]</span>
<span class="n">type</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&quot;choice&quot;</span>
<span class="n">question</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&quot;Which team should handle this support request?&quot;</span>

<span class="k">[decision.ticket-route.options]</span>
<span class="n">billing</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&quot;Billing or refunds&quot;</span>
<span class="n">engineering</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&quot;Technical problem or product bug&quot;</span>
<span class="n">sales</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&quot;Purchasing or procurement&quot;</span>
</pre></div>
</div>
<div class="highlight-bash notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span>pyjev<span class="w"> </span>decision<span class="w"> </span>validate
pyjev<span class="w"> </span>decision<span class="w"> </span>compile<span class="w"> </span>ticket-route<span class="w"> </span>--state<span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&quot;example ticket&quot;</span>
</pre></div>
</div>
<div class="highlight-python notranslate"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="kn">from</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nn">pyjev</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kn">import</span> <span class="n">Jev</span>
<span class="kn">from</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nn">pyjev.pipeline</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kn">import</span> <span class="n">require_confidence</span>

<span class="k">with</span> <span class="n">Jev</span><span class="p">()</span> <span class="k">as</span> <span class="n">jev</span><span class="p">:</span>
    <span class="n">route</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">jev</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">decide</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s2">&quot;ticket-route&quot;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">state</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="n">ticket</span><span class="p">)</span>

<span class="n">outcome</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">route</span> <span class="o">|</span> <span class="n">require_confidence</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mf">0.85</span><span class="p">)</span>
</pre></div>
</div>
<p>Both approaches ultimately make a TypeSafe System One request through the
official SDK. pyjev adds value when <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">ticket-route</span></code> is a reusable, inspectable
project contract with an offline compile/fingerprint path and shared Python/CLI
policy conventions. If it is just a one-off implementation detail, the direct
SDK call is simpler.</p>
</section>
<section id="when-the-sdk-alone-is-the-better-choice">
<h2>When the SDK alone is the better choice</h2>
<p>Use <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">typesafe-sdk</span></code> directly when:</p>
<ul class="simple">
<li><p>the application has only a few inline System One calls;</p></li>
<li><p>the questions are highly dynamic and do not benefit from a named contract;</p></li>
<li><p>shell/CI reuse or offline declaration validation is not needed;</p></li>
<li><p>no pyjev recipe matches the workflow;</p></li>
<li><p>the application already owns its policy, batch, and output layers;</p></li>
<li><p>low-level SDK request controls are needed; or</p></li>
<li><p>a TypeSafe primitive is not exposed by pyjev.</p></li>
</ul>
<p>For example, the current pyjev decision model covers Noul, Choice, Score, and
bundles of those primitives, not TypeSafe’s <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">Box</span></code> primitive. Direct SDK use is an
expected escape hatch, not a missing promise of SDK parity.</p>
</section>
<section id="what-pyjev-deliberately-does-not-own">
<h2>What pyjev deliberately does not own</h2>
<ul class="simple">
<li><p><strong>Transport and API compatibility:</strong> request execution, retries, authentication,
assets, API errors, and model/API compatibility remain with <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">typesafe-sdk</span></code>.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Every SDK feature:</strong> pyjev is not a complete wrapper for every primitive or
low-level request option. Use an injected SDK client or <code class="docutils literal notranslate"><span class="pre">jev.client</span></code> when you
need controls outside pyjev’s higher-level surface.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Universal policy:</strong> confidence and probability thresholds must be selected and
calibrated by the caller for the relevant consequences.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Application effects:</strong> recipes can return proposals and results, but callers
own authorization, handlers, and side effects.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Governance or guarantees:</strong> a decision fingerprint is not an audit trail,
tamper-proof control, or correctness guarantee.</p></li>
</ul>
<p>If all you need is to issue System One requests, use the SDK. Add pyjev when the
judgment itself needs to become a reusable, inspectable application contract or
workflow.</p>
</section>
</section>
</div>
<script data-sphinxpress-script="search" defer>
(function () {
  "use strict";

  function initForm(form) {
    var input = form.querySelector(".tool-search-input");
    var results = form.querySelector(".tool-search-results");
    var navList = form.parentElement
      ? form.parentElement.querySelector(".tool-nav-list")
      : null;
    if (!input || !results) {
      return;
    }
    var emptyText = form.getAttribute("data-search-empty") || "No matches.";
    var indexUrl = form.getAttribute("data-search-index");
    if (!indexUrl) {
      hideForm();
      return;
    }

    var indexEntries = null;
    var indexError = false;
    var pendingQuery = null;

    function hideForm() {
      form.style.display = "none";
    }

    function escapeHtml(value) {
      return value
        .replace(/&/g, "&amp;")
        .replace(/</g, "&lt;")
        .replace(/>/g, "&gt;")
        .replace(/"/g, "&quot;")
        .replace(/'/g, "&#39;");
    }

    function showEmpty() {
      results.innerHTML =
        '<p class="tool-search-empty">' + escapeHtml(emptyText) + "</p>";
      results.hidden = false;
      if (navList) {
        navList.hidden = true;
      }
    }

    function clearResults() {
      results.innerHTML = "";
      results.hidden = true;
      if (navList) {
        navList.hidden = false;
      }
    }

    function renderResults(entries, tokens) {
      if (!entries.length) {
        showEmpty();
        return;
      }
      var html = entries
        .map(function (entry) {
          var snippetHtml = renderSnippet(entry, tokens);
          var href = entry.url + "#sphinxpress-search-hit";
          return (
            '<li class="tool-search-result">' +
            '<a href="' +
            escapeHtml(href) +
            '">' +
            '<p class="tool-search-result-title">' +
            escapeHtml(entry.title) +
            "</p>" +
            '<p class="tool-search-result-snippet">' +
            snippetHtml +
            "</p>" +
            "</a>" +
            "</li>"
          );
        })
        .join("");
      results.innerHTML = html;
      results.hidden = false;
      if (navList) {
        navList.hidden = true;
      }
    }

    function renderSnippet(entry, tokens) {
      var source = entry.snippet || "";
      if (!source) {
        return "";
      }
      var lower = source.toLowerCase();
      var firstToken = tokens[0] || "";
      var idx = lower.indexOf(firstToken);
      if (idx < 0) {
        return escapeHtml(source);
      }
      var before = source.slice(0, idx);
      var match = source.slice(idx, idx + firstToken.length);
      var after = source.slice(idx + firstToken.length);
      return (
        escapeHtml(before) +
        "<mark>" +
        escapeHtml(match) +
        "</mark>" +
        escapeHtml(after)
      );
    }

    function runQuery(query) {
      if (!indexEntries) {
        return;
      }
      var tokens = query
        .toLowerCase()
        .split(/\s+/)
        .filter(function (token) {
          return token.length > 0;
        });
      if (!tokens.length) {
        clearResults();
        return;
      }
      var hits = [];
      for (var i = 0; i < indexEntries.length; i += 1) {
        var entry = indexEntries[i];
        if (!entry.sections || !entry.sections.length) {
          continue;
        }
        var matched = true;
        var score = 0;
        for (var t = 0; t < tokens.length; t += 1) {
          var token = tokens[t];
          var found = false;
          var tokenScore = 0;
          for (var s = 0; s < entry.sections.length; s += 1) {
            var section = entry.sections[s];
            var lowerText = section.lower || "";
            if (!lowerText) {
              continue;
            }
            var from = 0;
            while (from <= lowerText.length) {
              var foundAt = lowerText.indexOf(token, from);
              if (foundAt < 0) {
                break;
              }
              tokenScore += 1;
              from = foundAt + token.length;
            }
            if (tokenScore > 0) {
              found = true;
            }
          }
          if (!found) {
            matched = false;
            break;
          }
          score += tokenScore;
        }
        if (matched) {
          hits.push({ entry: entry, score: score });
        }
      }
      hits.sort(function (a, b) {
        return b.score - a.score;
      });
      var top = hits.slice(0, 20).map(function (hit) {
        return hit.entry;
      });
      renderResults(top, tokens);
    }

    function handleInput() {
      var query = input.value || "";
      if (!query.trim()) {
        clearResults();
        pendingQuery = null;
        return;
      }
      if (indexError) {
        hideForm();
        return;
      }
      if (indexEntries) {
        runQuery(query);
      } else {
        pendingQuery = query;
      }
    }

    input.addEventListener("input", handleInput);

    fetch(indexUrl, { credentials: "same-origin" })
      .then(function (response) {
        if (!response.ok) {
          throw new Error("HTTP " + response.status);
        }
        return response.json();
      })
      .then(function (payload) {
        if (
          !payload ||
          !Array.isArray(payload.entries) ||
          payload.entries.length === 0
        ) {
          hideForm();
          return;
        }
        indexEntries = payload.entries;
        if (pendingQuery) {
          runQuery(pendingQuery);
        }
      })
      .catch(function () {
        indexError = true;
        if (input.value && input.value.trim()) {
          hideForm();
        } else {
          hideForm();
        }
      });
  }

  function init() {
    var forms = document.querySelectorAll("form.tool-search");
    for (var i = 0; i < forms.length; i += 1) {
      initForm(forms[i]);
    }
  }

  if (document.readyState === "loading") {
    document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", init);
  } else {
    init();
  }
})();

</script>
{% endraw %}
